title: De Mortibus Persecutorum
author: Lactantius

passages.original: unde illum quidam deliri credunt esse translatum acuiuum reseruatum, Sibylla dicente matricidam profugum a finibus <terrae> esse uenturum, ut quia primus persecutus est, idem etiam nouissimus persequatur et antichristi praecedat aduentum — < quod n >efas est credere —, sicut duos prophetas uiuos esse translatos in ultima <tempora> ante imperium Christi sanctum ac sempiternum, cum descendere coeperit, < quidam sanctor >um pronuntient: eodem modo etiam Neronem uenturum putant, < ut praecu>rsor diaboli ac praeuius sit uenientis ad uastationem terrae et huma<ni ge>neris euersionem.
passages.english: For this reason certain madmen believe that he was carried away and kept alive, since the Sibyl says that a fugitive matricide will come from the ends of <the earth>, so that, because he was the first to persecute, he may also be the last to persecute and may precede the coming of the Antichrist (<which it is> wrong to believe), just as <certain of the saints> declare that two prophets were carried away alive to the last <times>, before the holy and everlasting reign of Christ, when he begins to descend: in the same way they think that Nero too will come, <so as to be the fore>runner of the devil and go before him as he comes for the devastation of the earth and the overthrow of the human <race>.
passages.notes: 'acuiuum' is read as 'ac uiuum' (a word-division error). Words in angle brackets are editorial supplements to a damaged text. The 'two prophets' are presumably Enoch and Elijah; the text does not name them.
